course.eras.broom.chapter.desc: The sweep arm passes over a whole run of cells, so the number of ways in is no longer fixed.
course.eras.broom.chapter.title: Many ways in
course.eras.paper.chapter.desc: Build the answer to a big problem out of the answers to small ones.
course.eras.paper.chapter.title: Pen and paper
course.eras.ranger.chapter.desc: It sees further, two cells away; it sees more, the two words a table compares; and it can scan the other way round.
course.eras.ranger.chapter.title: Seeing further
course.eras.reach.chapter.desc: A telescopic arm reaches a cell however far away.
course.eras.reach.chapter.title: A longer arm
course.eras.scout.chapter.desc: On every cell the robot runs the same circuit board, and a finished board becomes a component.
course.eras.scout.chapter.title: Build a machine
course.eras.settle.chapter.desc: When the arrows loop round, scan again and again.
course.eras.settle.chapter.title: Scan until it settles
course.eras.stack.chapter.desc: When one number can’t remember enough, remember one more thing.
course.eras.stack.chapter.title: When the state falls short
game.description: 状态之图 State Graph：零基础动态规划解谜游戏。Dynamic programming puzzles for complete beginners.
game.lede: No programming or algorithms background needed. Starting from counting routes by hand, you learn to break a big problem into a table and fill it in cell by cell; in the end you wire up the circuit boards that count routes, compare words and pack a backpack, and see why they are so fast.
game.title: State Graph
glossary.entries.brief.body.0: The first time you enter a level, a few pages of Intro open first, explaining the level’s new problem and anything new in it. To read them again, click “Intro” in the top bar; on a computer, ← and → turn the pages.
glossary.entries.brief.body.1: In the level’s brief, the Goal says what the level wants worked out, and How to play says what you have to do. When you are stuck, read the goal again first.
glossary.entries.brief.body.2: Some levels come in several stages, asking a few questions in a row about the same map; some stages hand their circuit board on to the next.
glossary.entries.brief.body.3: Not every level needs a circuit: in some you draw arrows, fill in numbers or trace routes on the board by hand, and “How to play” says which.
glossary.entries.brief.title: Intro, goal and how to play
glossary.entries.map.body.0: The levels sit on the map in chapters, and each chapter answers one question. Pass a level and the levels after it open; where the path splits, take the branches in any order, and pass them all to go on.
glossary.entries.map.body.1: The map also has your Parts and this Encyclopedia.
glossary.entries.map.title: Level map
glossary.entries.models.body.0: Each level decides which robot model it uses. The first time a new model turns up, the Intro introduces it.
glossary.entries.models.body.1: The biggest difference between models is their vision. Boxy sees the ring of cells around it, 3×3; Farsight sees two rings, 5×5. A circuit board can only read cells in view, so reading further takes a different model.
glossary.entries.models.title: Robot models
glossary.entries.robot.body.0: In circuit-board levels the computing is done by a robot. It walks the whole table cell by cell, runs the same circuit board on every cell, and writes the result into the cell it stands on.
glossary.entries.robot.body.1: The red frame in the middle of the robot’s view is the cell it stands on. For the circuit board to read a cell in view, click it in the view: the “View” part on the left of the circuit board gains an output that reads it, and a cell being read has a blue frame in the view. Cells beyond the table show “out”, and what they send is “—”.
glossary.entries.robot.body.2: The This cell panel under the view lists facts about the cell. Click one, and the “This cell” part gains an output that reads it.
glossary.entries.robot.title: The robot and its view
glossary.entries.robotBoard.body.0: Connect an output from View or Cell Info to a computation part, then wire the result to the write-back port. The robot runs the board again at each cell.
glossary.entries.robotBoard.body.1: After wiring the board, switch tests to check the results across the table. If only a few cells are wrong, start by looking at what the robot reads at those cells.
glossary.entries.robotBoard.title: The robot’s circuit board
